subject: plot phenotypes versus 3 SNP genotypes at particular SNP

messages.author: 68d73cc05e36688d
messages.subject: plot phenotypes versus 3 SNP genotypes at particular SNP
parts:
Hi Karl

Thanks for your previous help. I now have another question:
I used the function plot_pxg() to plot the phenotypes at a particular QTL across the 36 diplotypes. But what I would like to do is to plot the phenotypes versus the 3 SNP genotypes (AA, AB, BB) and also get this genotype information for each mouse ID.

Thanks in advance!

Kind regards
Jacky

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] plot phenotypes versus 3 SNP genotypes at particular SNP
parts:
You could use the function predict_snpgeno() to collapse inferred diplotypes into SNP genotypes, based on the founders' SNP genotypes.
See the example in the help file for predict_snpgeno():
	file <- paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rqtl/",
        	       "qtl2data/master/DOex/DOex.zip")
	DOex <- read_cross2(file)
	probs <- calc_genoprob(DOex, error_prob=0.002)

	# inferred genotypes
	m <- maxmarg(probs, minprob=0.5)

	# inferred SNP genotypes
	inferg <- predict_snpgeno(DOex, m)

Alternatively, you can collapse the genotype probabilities to SNP probabilities using genoprob_to_snpprob() and then use maxmarg() with those probabilities.

	# convert diplotype probabilities to SNP genotype probabilities
	snp_probs <- genoprob_to_snpprob(probs, DOex)

	# get inferred SNP genotypes at a particular position
	inferg <- maxmarg(snp_probs, DOex$pmap, chr=2, pos=96.842, return_char=TRUE)

	# plot phenotype vs inferred SNP genotype
	plot_pxg(inferg, DOex$pheno)

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] plot phenotypes versus 3 SNP genotypes at particular SNP
parts:
It does happen that there can be selection for one particular founder in a region, and against some other founder.

I don't see how reduce_markers() would be useful in this case.
And the error that you're getting doesn't make much sense to me. Can you provide the full code that you're using?
If you want just the marker names from the output of reduce_markers(), you could do:

reduced_map <- reduce_markers(gmap, 1)
reduced_markers <- unlist( lapply(reduced_map, names) )

You could then use

reduced_cross <- pull_markers(mycross, reduced_markers)

I wouldn't eliminate markers with high or low parental allele frequencies. If they reflect what's going on in the population, then you wouldn't want to eliminate them.

karl
